name: Yusuf Hasan
bio: Yusuf Hasan came to the UK from Pakistan as a young man and spent most of his working life behind the wheel of a cab. Thousands of fares, thousands of conversations, and somewhere along the way he realised the back seat had taught him more than any classroom could.

Now retired, he keeps busy the only way he knows how, by writing. His first two books grew out of the lessons he picked up on the road, about patience, grief, forgiveness and the strange honesty of strangers. He has carried on since then with fiction and human interest stories, always with the same aim: to pass on what he has learnt, and to keep learning as he goes.
Yusuf lives in the UK. He still believes everyone has a story worth hearing, if you take the time to ask.

books.title: Any Other Business
books.description: A character-driven contemporary novel attentive to ordinary lives and their unexpected complications. It explores how the business of daily survival intersects with relationships and personal ambition.

books.title: The Fare
books.description: A warm, affecting novel about the lessons learned from the back seat of a taxi. Through encounters with passengers, it explores empathy, human connection and the unexpected wisdom of ordinary journeys.
books.long: For twenty-three years London cab driver Yusuf Hasan has listened as passengers reveal what they cannot say elsewhere. Seventeen memorable journeys bring him face to face with grief, courage, love and forgiveness, including a widow, an absent brother and a bride who walks away from her wedding. His greatest challenge, however, is applying to his own life the wisdom he has offered so freely to strangers.

books.title: The Empty Cab
books.description: A poignant companion to The Fare that returns to the world of taxi journeys and the lives encountered along the way. It considers absence, memory and the stories that stay with us after a ride ends.
books.long: After twenty-three years driving a London taxi, Yusuf Hasan retires in the shadow of an irregular heart rhythm he has concealed behind a confident farewell. Without passengers, routine or the role that made him feel needed, he must confront changes in marriage, family and identity. Visits to old colleagues and a long-estranged brother in Canada turn retirement into a difficult, moving journey from listening to other people’s truths towards telling his own.

books.title: Paid in Full
books.description: A contemporary novel exploring what people owe, what they sacrifice and what it means to settle a debt. Its questions reach beyond money to responsibility, loyalty and personal redemption.

books.title: Sorry, We're Open
books.description: A warm British family comedy set around a Newcastle corner shop. Amid the demands of customers, family and daily survival, it celebrates resilience, community and the absurdity of everyday life.

name: Dr. Yusuf Al-Qalb
bio: Dr. Yusuf Al-Qalb writes Islamic non-fiction. His 15 books include the ten-booklet Returning to Allah series, covering du'a, sabr, gratitude and more, as well as Before You Go, a guide to preparing for death, The Man They Could Not Stop, on the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), and The Daily Heart, a year of daily reflections and journaling.

books.title: Before You Go
books.description: A reflective invitation to consider life, mortality and the legacy we leave behind. Drawing on Islamic values, it encourages readers to prepare the heart as thoughtfully as they plan their days.

books.title: Who Runs the Mosque?
books.description: An accessible look at leadership, responsibility and community life within the mosque. It raises important questions about governance, inclusion and the difference between serving an institution and serving its people.
books.long: An investigation of how mosques and Islamic institutions in Britain are governed, funded and held accountable. Yusuf Al-Qalb examines trusteeship, property ownership, cash handling, safeguarding, the employment of imams, representation and community disputes. Alongside its critique, the book offers practical tools for reading accounts, asking questions at AGMs and strengthening transparent, trusted institutions.

books.title: The Hive That Forgot How to Build
books.description: Using the image of a hive, this book considers what happens when a community loses sight of cooperation and shared purpose. A call to rebuild collective responsibility through faith, service and practical action.

books.title: The Man They Could Not Stop
books.description: An engaging exploration of the life, resilience and extraordinary influence of Prophet Muhammad. It reflects on how his message endured opposition and continues to shape lives and communities.
books.long: A fresh account of the life and influence of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), viewed through the hostility and opposition of his most determined adversaries. It considers why efforts to halt his mission failed and how resilience, conviction and the power of his message changed the course of history.

books.title: Still Your Heart
books.description: A gentle Islamic guide to finding calm amid worry, distraction and uncertainty. It invites readers to recover inner steadiness through remembrance, reflection and trust in Allah.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 1 of 10

books.title: Wait With Grace
books.description: A thoughtful Islamic perspective on delays, disappointment and unanswered prayers. It offers encouragement for cultivating patience without surrendering hope or meaningful action.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 2 of 10

books.title: Raise Your Hands
books.description: An accessible meditation on du’a, the intimate act of turning to Allah in prayer. It explores sincerity, hope and the strength found in asking, waiting and trusting.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 3 of 10

books.title: Come Back
books.description: A compassionate invitation to reconnect with Allah, regardless of how distant faith may feel. Centred on hope and repentance, it explores the possibility of beginning again.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 4 of 10

books.title: Count Your Blessings
books.description: A practical, uplifting exploration of gratitude as an everyday spiritual discipline. It encourages readers to notice ordinary gifts and respond with humility, contentment and generosity.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 5 of 10

books.title: Polish the Mirror
books.description: An invitation to examine and refine the inner self through Islamic reflection. It explores sincerity, character and the daily work of clearing away habits that cloud the heart.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 6 of 10

books.title: Pack Light
books.description: A reflective guide to loosening attachment to what weighs down the heart. Through an Islamic lens, it considers simplicity, priorities and preparing for what matters beyond this life.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 7 of 10

books.title: Enough
books.description: A searching reflection on the grip of dunya, the distractions and desires of worldly life. It asks what true sufficiency looks like when measured against faith and lasting purpose.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 8 of 10

books.title: Trust the Plan
books.description: A faith-centred reflection on uncertainty, patience and divine wisdom. It encourages readers to act with purpose while accepting that not every outcome is theirs to control.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 9 of 10

books.title: Before You Sleep
books.description: A quiet, contemplative companion for the close of each day. It encourages reflection, gratitude, repentance and a more intentional relationship with Allah.
books.series: Returning to Allah, Islamic Spiritual Series, Booklet 10 of 10

books.title: The Daily Heart
books.description: A year-long collection of daily prompts and spiritual reflections for Muslim readers. Each entry creates space to pause, write and strengthen the connection between belief and daily practice.

name: Dr. Syed Ali Akbar Rizvi
bio: Dr. Syed Ali Akbar Rizvi writes both non-fiction and fiction. His non-fiction includes a journey through Nahjul Balagha, a look at the prophets shared by the Bible and the Qur'an, and 365 days of reflections. His novels include The Lost and Found and its sequel, Ninety Days More.

books.title: The Light of Divine Wisdom
books.description: An exploration of enduring ethical and spiritual insights associated with Nahj al-Balagha. It invites readers to reflect on wisdom, character, justice and the responsibilities of human life.

books.title: Conversations with Allah the Al-Samīʿ
books.description: A contemplative journey into speaking to Allah with honesty, vulnerability and hope. Grounded in the divine name Al-Samīʿ, the All-Hearing, it reflects on the comfort of being heard.

books.title: Shared Light
books.description: A reflective work about the values and spiritual insights that connect people across apparent differences. It encourages dialogue, empathy and the recognition of common humanity.

books.title: The 5 Intoxicants
books.description: A thought-provoking work of fiction examining the forces that captivate human desires and distort choices. Through its central idea of five intoxicants, it explores temptation, freedom and self-knowledge.
books.long: Beginning with an encounter in seventh-century Kufa, this reflective work identifies five forces that can cloud judgement: wealth, power, knowledge, praise and youth. Combining Islamic thought with Stoic philosophy and contemporary psychology, it explains how admirable pursuits become dangerous when they control identity and ambition. Practical reflections invite readers to reconsider success and cultivate clarity and purpose.

books.title: The Lost and Found
books.description: A reflective novel about loss, identity and the unexpected ways people find their way back to themselves. Its emotional centre is the possibility that what is missing may lead to something new.

books.title: Ninety Days More
books.description: A novel confronting the meaning of time when its limits become impossible to ignore. It explores what relationships, regrets and unfinished hopes reveal about a life worth living.
books.series: Sequel to The Lost and Found

name: Sage Norden, PhD
bio: Sage Norden, PhD writes non-fiction on politics, power and technology. The seven books so far cover AI and layoffs, American foreign policy, Britain's problems, the surveillance economy and the cost of telling the truth.

books.title: The Jobs We Blamed on Machines
books.description: A provocative examination of automation and the changing world of work. It questions whether machines alone are responsible for lost jobs, or whether human choices play the greater role.
books.long: Sage Norden challenges the corporate claim that layoffs are the inevitable result of artificial intelligence. The book investigates how automation can become a convenient explanation for cost-cutting strategies and management choices already in motion. It asks readers to separate genuine technological change from the financial incentives and decisions that determine whose jobs disappear.

books.title: The Ally We Never Question
books.description: An examination of political alliances and the assumptions that sustain them. It asks what governments and citizens overlook when strategic partnerships escape meaningful scrutiny.

books.title: The Governments We Unmade
books.description: A critical look at the consequences of foreign intervention and political upheaval. It considers what follows when outside powers help dismantle governments but cannot control what comes next.

books.title: The Dictators We Love
books.description: A challenging exploration of why powerful nations sometimes embrace authoritarian leaders. It exposes the tension between proclaimed democratic values and strategic convenience.

books.title: The Country That Stopped Learning
books.description: An argument about the costs of institutional stagnation and resistance to evidence. It explores what happens when a society loses its ability to question, adapt and learn.

books.title: Owned
books.description: A critique of the surveillance economy and the trade-offs hidden in digital convenience. It examines data, power and the gradual erosion of personal autonomy.

books.title: The Comfort Tax
books.description: A thought-provoking analysis of what modern convenience really costs. It looks beyond price tags to ask how comfort reshapes autonomy, expectations and public life.

name: Julian Vale
bio: Julian Vale is the author of 14 novels, including The Island of Second Chances, The Last Train Before Morning, The Ferryman Who Never Crossed and The Other Chair.

books.title: The Island of Second Chances
books.description: A philosophical novel set around the tantalising possibility of beginning again. It asks whether a new chance can change a life without changing the person who lives it.
books.long: Seven strangers arrive on a mysterious island, each haunted by one moment they desperately wish to change. Offered the extraordinary opportunity to revisit that decision, they must confront both the possibility of redemption and the cost of choosing differently. A philosophical, emotionally driven novel about guilt, responsibility and whether a second chance can truly remake a life.

books.title: The Last Train Before Morning
books.description: A mysterious, reflective journey in which travel becomes a way of confronting unfinished choices. It explores regret, possibility and the destinations people never expected to reach.
books.long: After her mother’s funeral and on the eve of her wedding, forty-one-year-old Elena boards an overnight train carrying a letter she is afraid to open. Fellow passengers share experiences of grief, compromise and missed possibilities, unsettling her certainty about the life she has chosen. As dawn approaches, Elena must ask whether her safe future is genuinely hers or simply an escape from the alternatives.

books.title: The Ferryman
books.description: A metaphysical tale built around passage, transition and the questions people carry across thresholds. It considers what must be faced before anyone can truly move on.

books.title: The Gardener of Forgotten Dreams
books.description: A lyrical fantasy about neglected ambitions and the dreams people set aside. It imagines what might happen when forgotten possibilities are given the chance to grow again.

books.title: The Shop That Sold Lost Things
books.description: A whimsical, philosophical novel centred on the emotional value of things people lose. It explores memory, longing and the unexpected cost of getting something back.

books.title: The Library of Unwritten Lives
books.description: A speculative novel about stories never lived and the choices that create them. It invites readers to consider the alternate selves that remain just beyond reach.
books.long: Owen Meilor, a struggling writer whose marriage and ambitions have unravelled, discovers an impossible library containing truthful books about individual lives. His own volume records everything until the present, after which its pages are blank. Reading the lives of strangers forces Owen to reconsider failure, regret and the frightening freedom of a future that has not yet been written.

books.title: The Man Who Collected Tomorrows
books.description: An imaginative story about the allure of possible futures. It explores the tension between wanting to know what comes next and learning to live in the present.

books.title: The Man Who Gave Away His Name
books.description: A philosophical tale about identity, belonging and what remains when the labels defining us disappear. It questions how much of a person can be surrendered without losing the self.

books.title: The House With Seven Doors
books.description: A metaphysical novel using the mystery of seven doors to explore different possibilities and decisions. Each threshold suggests a new way of thinking about the life we choose.

books.title: The Castle at the End of the Road
books.description: A standalone literary novel with an atmosphere of mystery and philosophical inquiry. It follows the pull of an enigmatic destination and the personal questions raised along the way.
books.long: Exhausted by a lifetime of solving everyone else’s problems, a successful fifty-year-old buys a remote castle hotel in the Scottish Highlands, hoping to become unnecessary for once. The manager, his wife and an unpredictable stream of guests challenge his habit of rescuing others. A humane, reflective novel about marriage, ageing, boundaries and learning that being loved is not the same as being useful.

books.title: The Garden Across the Street
books.description: A quietly resonant standalone novel about the lives we observe and the stories we assume. It finds emotional meaning in proximity, memory and unexpected connection.

books.title: The Clockmaker Who Stopped Time
books.description: A thought-provoking fantasy about time, control and the desire to hold on to fleeting moments. It asks whether stopping change would preserve life or diminish it.

books.title: The Uncollected
books.description: When Tess inherits her grandmother Edie’s Scottish alterations shop, a long-buried mystery emerges from the seams of a wedding dress. A moving literary novel about family secrets, memory and what we carry forward.
books.long: After a career setback, Tess Marsh inherits her grandmother’s alterations shop in a small village on a Scottish loch and plans to close it quickly. Returning forty uncollected garments reveals intimate stories of the community and unexpected truths about her grandmother. A mysterious forty-first ticket leads Tess towards an old family secret and a new understanding of home, belonging and second chances.

books.title: The Other Chair
books.description: An introspective literary novel that uses the presence, or absence, of another person to explore connection and identity. A story interested in the silences that shape a life.
books.long: Newcastle psychologist Clare Ashby is skilled at helping patients with grief, fear and strained relationships, but one session unsettles a secret she has kept for eleven years. As professional boundaries blur, Clare travels every Thursday to a room overlooking the North Sea to confront a painful memory of her own sister. An intimate novel about the limits of advice, unresolved guilt and the burden carried by those who care for others.

name: James Whitfield
bio: James Whitfield is the author of Still Standing, a calm, practical guide to keeping your job and your nerve as AI changes the way we work.

books.title: Still Standing: Keep Your Job
books.description: A pragmatic guide to adapting at work as artificial intelligence transforms employment. It focuses on resilience, relevant skills and protecting professional value amid technological change.
books.long: A practical guide for experienced professionals who fear that artificial intelligence may make their skills obsolete. James Whitfield shows how to assess workplace changes, strengthen professional value, use AI without abandoning judgement and build networks before a crisis arises. Actionable steps help readers choose when to adapt, negotiate or move on rather than allowing anxiety to dictate their careers.

name: Eleanor Hart
bio: Eleanor Hart writes fiction and non-fiction. Her novels include the first three books of the Meridian Sequence (The Weight of Light, All the Distance Between and The Ordinary Infinite) and Almost. Her non-fiction title is Estranged by Choice, on cutting off parents.

books.title: Weight of Light
books.description: A literary exploration of grief, hope and the paradoxes of human connection. Its central tension lies in how even moments of beauty can carry emotional weight.
books.long: When astronomer Dr Lena Kasra detects an impossible pulse repeating every 4.7 seconds, she joins the survey ship Meridian to trace its source. On board, Captain Yuna Shin and a crew shaped by personal loss face the strains of trust and discovery. The first Meridian Sequence novel blends scientifically grounded first-contact mystery with intimate questions about grief and the human cost of reaching across 27.8 light-years.

books.title: All the Distance Between
books.description: An emotionally observant novel about separation and the ties that endure across it. It considers what distance does to memory, relationships and the things left unsaid.
books.long: Years after the first signal from 61 Virginis, Lena Kasra faces the daunting delay of a conversation measured in decades rather than minutes. Joined by a xenolinguist and new crew members, she discovers that communication with another intelligence is less like translating words and more like negotiating understanding. Book two of the Meridian Sequence explores waiting, sacrifice, grief and the possibility that some distances cannot be eliminated.

books.title: The Ordinary Infinite
books.description: A literary novel that finds extraordinary significance in seemingly ordinary experience. It explores the intersections of time, intimacy and the hidden depth of everyday life.
books.long: In the closing volume of the Meridian Sequence, scientist Lena Kasra and the crew of Meridian II finally approach an encounter with the surviving consciousness of an ancient civilisation. The long journey brings unresolved questions of sacrifice, grief and belonging to the forefront. This reflective science-fiction finale asks whether the greatest barrier in first contact is distance in space or the difficulty of understanding another mind.

books.title: Almost
books.description: A tender novel about near misses, unrealised possibilities and the lives that might have been. It reflects on the lasting influence of choices made and choices deferred.

books.title: Estranged by Choice
books.description: A nuanced nonfiction exploration of intentional family estrangement and the difficult decisions behind it. It considers boundaries, guilt, healing and the complexity of rebuilding a life on one’s own terms.

name: Dev Malhotra
bio: Dev Malhotra is the author of The Trouble with Us, on what South Asians and the British get right, wrong and completely misunderstand about each other.

books.title: The Trouble with Us
books.description: A candid, humorous look at what British and South Asian cultures get right, wrong and spectacularly misunderstand about one another. From family and hospitality to identity and social expectations, it finds insight in the friction.

name: Anna Wray
bio: Anna Wray is the author of the Dr Claire Shaw novels: The Patient Who Never Lied (Book One), The Good Husband (Book Two) and What the Patient Knew (Book Three).

books.title: The Patient Who Never Lied
books.description: The opening psychological mystery in the Dr Claire Shaw series, where clinical observation meets hidden truths. Set against the atmosphere of West Yorkshire, it explores how appearances can mislead even a perceptive professional.

books.title: The Good Husband
books.description: A Dr Claire Shaw psychological mystery examining the unsettling gap between a respectable public image and private reality. The novel probes trust, relationships and the stories people choose to believe.

books.title: What the Patient Knew
books.description: In this Dr Claire Shaw mystery, knowledge can be as dangerous as concealment. A psychologically driven story about secrets, perception and the consequences of what a patient reveals.

name: Adam Yusuf
bio: Adam Yusuf is the author of The First Year, an honest guide to life after the shahada for new Muslims and everyone who loves one.

books.title: The First Year
books.description: A practical, reassuring companion to the first year of Muslim life and spiritual growth. It explores the habits, questions and everyday decisions that help faith become a lasting part of life.
books.long: Following the shahada, new Muslims face a year of practical, emotional and spiritual adjustments that introductory guides seldom address. Adam Yusuf discusses learning to pray, navigating conflicting advice, explaining conversion to family, separating religion from culture, encountering the mosque community and experiencing a first Ramadan. The book reassures readers that uncertainty, slow progress and honest questions can all be part of building a lasting Muslim life.

name: Dr. Saiyed Ali Al-Razavi
bio: Dr. Saiyed Ali Al-Razavi writes non-fiction on Shia Islam. His 10 books include histories such as The Field of Karbala and Tears of the Ummah, guides such as The Shia Muslim Handbook and Raising Shia Children in the West, and Whispers to the Divine, a guide to popular Shia supplications.

books.title: The Field of Karbala
books.description: A reflection on Karbala as a defining event of sacrifice, conscience and resistance to injustice. It considers the enduring moral and spiritual meanings of Imam Husayn’s stand.
books.long: This historical account reconstructs the political crises leading to the death of Husayn ibn Ali at Karbala in 680 CE. From succession disputes and the rise of the Umayyads to the promises of Kufa, the battle and Zaynab’s testimony, it distinguishes early evidence from later devotional traditions. It asks what Karbala reveals about conscience, obedience, political power and the moral significance of refusing unjust authority.

books.title: Daughters of Revelation
books.description: An exploration of the women whose courage, knowledge and devotion illuminate Islamic history. It brings their significance into focus and considers the lessons their lives offer today.

books.title: Raising Shia Children in the West
books.description: A practical guide to nurturing Shia identity and values while raising children in Western societies. It addresses the balance between belonging, confidence, faith education and everyday family life.

books.title: Understanding the Twelve Imams
books.description: An approachable introduction to the Twelve Imams in Shia Islam and their religious significance. It explores their place in a tradition of spiritual leadership, scholarship and moral example.

books.title: The Shia Muslim Handbook
books.description: A reader-friendly introduction to the beliefs, practices and everyday questions of Shia Muslim life. Designed to make foundational concepts accessible without losing their spiritual depth.

books.title: The Next Marja
books.description: A timely examination of religious authority and leadership within contemporary Shia Islam. It considers how scholarship, trust and the needs of changing communities shape discussions of marja‘iyya.

books.title: The Shia Islam You've Heard About
books.description: A thoughtful response to common assumptions and misconceptions about Shia Islam. It aims to replace slogans and second-hand impressions with context, nuance and understanding.

books.title: Understanding the Shia
books.description: A clear introduction to Shia history, beliefs and religious identity for curious readers. It offers context for both shared Islamic foundations and distinctive traditions.

books.title: Tears of the Ummah
books.description: A reflective look at sorrow, solidarity and the moral responsibilities of the Muslim community. It explores how grief can become compassion, remembrance and commitment to justice.

books.title: Whispers to the Divine
books.description: An intimate collection of reflections on prayer, longing and closeness to Allah. It draws readers toward the quieter, more personal dimensions of spiritual life.
